```{r}
#| label: setup
for (path in sort(list.files("../R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE))) {
  source(path, local = FALSE)
}

quiet_theme <- ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#333333")
  )
```

## Scenario

This is a deterministic, explanatory simulation shaped like the planned
Judbury design: 30 candidate species, 20 true grid members, nine cameras and
208 seven-day occasions. All operational outages are synthetic. This is not
estimator validation or an empirical Judbury fit, and no empirical camera data
are used.

```{r}
#| label: simulate
config <- flexirich_sim_config(seed = 20260723L)
sim <- simulate_flexirich_g(config)
validate_flexirich_sim(sim)

sim_summary <- summary(sim)
curve <- discovery_curve(sim)
detection_frequency <- sim$detections |>
  dplyr::group_by(species_id, member) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sampled_camera_weeks = sum(sampled),
    detected_camera_weeks = sum(detected == 1L, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    detection_frequency = detected_camera_weeks / sampled_camera_weeks,
    membership_label = factor(
      member,
      levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
      labels = c("Not a true grid member", "True grid member")
    )
  )

stopifnot(
  identical(config$candidate_pool_size, 30L),
  identical(config$true_richness, 20L),
  identical(config$n_cameras, 9L),
  identical(config$n_occasions, 208L),
  identical(config$occasion_days, 7L),
  identical(config$seed, 20260723L),
  sim_summary$observed_richness >= 0L,
  sim_summary$observed_richness <= sim_summary$true_richness,
  identical(sim_summary$true_richness, 20L),
  length(unique(sim$effort_weekly$camera_id)) == 9L,
  all(sim$effort_weekly$active_days %in% 0:7),
  any(sim$effort_weekly$active_days < 7L),
  all(is.finite(sim$rates$encounter_rate)),
  all(sim$rates$encounter_rate > 0),
  diff(range(sim$rates$encounter_rate)) > 0,
  all(detection_frequency$sampled_camera_weeks > 0L),
  all(
    detection_frequency$detected_camera_weeks <=
      detection_frequency$sampled_camera_weeks
  ),
  all(detection_frequency$detection_frequency >= 0),
  all(detection_frequency$detection_frequency <= 1),
  nrow(curve) == 208L,
  all(diff(curve$cumulative_richness) >= 0L),
  all(curve$cumulative_richness <= sim$truth$true_richness),
  identical(
    tail(curve$cumulative_richness, 1L),
    sim$truth$observed_richness
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  sim_summary,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Deterministic scenario summary"
)
```

## Operational effort

```{r}
#| label: fig-effort
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap of active days per week for nine synthetic cameras over 208 weekly occasions, with lighter cells showing simulated outages."
effort_plot_data <- sim$effort_weekly |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    camera_id = factor(camera_id, levels = rev(unique(camera_id)))
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  effort_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = occasion_start, y = camera_id, fill = active_days)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(width = 7, height = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#f7fbff",
    high = "#08519c",
    limits = c(0, 7),
    breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 6, 7)
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "6 months",
    date_labels = "%b\n%Y",
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Weekly occasion start",
    y = "Synthetic camera",
    fill = "Active days\nper week",
    title = "Weekly operational effort across nine synthetic cameras",
    subtitle = "Lighter cells show synthetic outages; full operation is 7 active camera-days."
  ) +
  quiet_theme +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

## Species encounter heterogeneity

Membership is assigned independently of encounter-rate effects in the
simulator. The membership-coloured rug marks below are therefore descriptive
labels only, not a causal or fitted group comparison.

```{r}
#| label: fig-rates
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-alt: "Histogram on a logarithmic horizontal scale showing heterogeneous positive baseline encounter rates for 30 candidate species, with rug marks identifying independently assigned membership labels."
species_plot_data <- sim$species |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    baseline_rate = exp(alpha),
    membership_label = factor(
      member,
      levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
      labels = c("Not a true grid member", "True grid member")
    )
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  species_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = baseline_rate)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(
    bins = 12,
    fill = "#8aa6b8",
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_rug(
    ggplot2::aes(colour = membership_label),
    linewidth = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10() +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Not a true grid member" = "#6b6b6b",
      "True grid member" = "#245b8a"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Baseline encounter rate per active camera-day (log scale)",
    y = "Candidate species per bin",
    colour = "Simulation label",
    title = "Positive, heterogeneous baseline encounter rates",
    subtitle = "Membership is independent by design; rug colours label this draw only."
  ) +
  quiet_theme
```

## Binary-detection frequency

For each candidate species, the numerator is the number of sampled camera-week
cells with a binary detection and the denominator is the number of camera-week
cells with at least one active day. Zero-effort cells are excluded rather than
treated as non-detections.

```{r}
#| label: fig-detection-frequency
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal dot plot of observed binary-detection frequency for each of 30 candidate species, calculated over camera-week cells with positive operational effort."
detection_plot_data <- detection_frequency |>
  dplyr::arrange(detection_frequency, species_id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    species_id = factor(species_id, levels = species_id)
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  detection_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(y = species_id)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = 0,
      xend = detection_frequency,
      yend = species_id
    ),
    colour = "#d9d9d9",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = detection_frequency,
      colour = membership_label,
      shape = membership_label
    ),
    size = 2.4
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Not a true grid member" = "#6b6b6b",
      "True grid member" = "#245b8a"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Not a true grid member" = 1,
      "True grid member" = 16
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Detected sampled camera-weeks (%)",
    y = "Candidate species",
    colour = "Simulation label",
    shape = "Simulation label",
    title = "Observed binary-detection frequency by candidate species",
    subtitle = "Nonmembers have structural zero detection by design.",
    caption = paste(
      "Frequency = detected camera-weeks / camera-weeks with positive effort;",
      "zero-effort cells are excluded."
    )
  ) +
  quiet_theme +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )
```

## Discovery trajectory

```{r}
#| label: fig-discovery
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-alt: "Chronological step plot of cumulative observed richness over 208 simulated weekly occasions, with a dashed horizontal reference at the known true richness of 20."
ggplot2::ggplot(
  curve,
  ggplot2::aes(x = occasion_start, y = cumulative_richness)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = sim$truth$true_richness,
    colour = "#777777",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_step(
    colour = "#1f4e79",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "6 months",
    date_labels = "%b\n%Y"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, sim$truth$true_richness, by = 5),
    limits = c(0, sim$truth$true_richness + 1),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Weekly occasion start",
    y = "Cumulative observed richness",
    title = "Cumulative species discovery through 208 simulated weeks",
    subtitle = "Dark blue is observed discovery; dashed grey is the known true richness (20)."
  ) +
  quiet_theme
```

## Acceptance interpretation

For this deterministic draw, the final cumulative discovery count agrees with
the observed-richness summary and does not exceed the known true richness. The
figures make synthetic effort gaps, encounter-rate heterogeneity and discovery
timing inspectable. They do not show that any richness estimator is unbiased,
calibrated or robust to misspecification; no estimator is fitted here.
